title: VASP association stabilizes the actin nucleus revealed by molecular dynamics simulations
abstract: Actin nucleation is a rate-limiting step in F-actin assembly. However, early actin trimers are intrinsically unstable, with limited inter-subunit contacts rendering them prone to dissociation. VASP is an important regulator of actin polymerization and assembly, but how it stabilizes unstable trimeric actin nucleus remains poorly understood at the molecular level. Here, we use coarse-grained and all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the interfacial stability and conformational features of VASP-bound actin trimers. Energetic and interfacial analyses show that VASP preferentially anchors the laterally associated subunit through multivalent interactions and reinforces its interfaces with the longitudinal actin dimer. Within the VASP-bound trimer, the three actin subunits retain distinct local conformational features, as reflected by differences in W-loop gating and SD1-to-SD4 dihedral angle. Across replicate simulations, VASP stabilizes the actin nucleus while preserving subunit-specific conformational heterogeneity, rather than uniformly rigidifying the trimer. These findings provide a molecular basis for VASP-mediated stabilization of early actin nuclei and offer broader mechanistic insights into the regulation of protein assembly.
relevance_reason: Coarse-grained and all-atom MD simulations of VASP-bound actin trimers satisfy (a)-(c) by simulating explicit atomic/CG systems to characterize interfacial stability.

title: To mix or to de-mix?: Cation-π suppresses heterogeneity in local structure and dynamics of heterotypic Condensates
abstract: Heterotypic biomolecular condensates can exhibit pronounced spatial and dynamic heterogeneity because chemically distinct components compete between self- and cross-association. Here, we use coarse-grained simulations to investigate how cation-{pi} interactions modulate this competition in condensates formed by peptides with systematic variation of hydrophobicity-to-charge ratios in binary peptide pairs. By independently tuning sequence heterogeneity, peptide composition, and cation-{pi} interaction strength, we establish how an additional short-range interaction reshapes condensate stability, internal organization, and molecular dynamics. In the absence of cation-{pi} interactions, highly heterogeneous peptide pairs form distinct core-shell architectures, with charge- and hydrophobicity-rich sequences preferentially occupying different regions of the condensate. Introducing cation-{pi} interactions progressively enhances phase stability and promotes molecular mixing, with stronger interactions substantially increasing the critical temperature and condensate density. Energetic analysis reveals that cation-{pi} interactions partially compensate for the loss of electrostatic and hydrophobic stabilization, providing an additional and tuneable source of cohesive interactions. This enhanced cross-association also suppresses spatial and dynamic heterogeneity, yielding more homogeneous peptide distributions, slower translational diffusion, and more uniform chain reconfiguration within the dense phase. Collectively, our results demonstrate that cation-{pi} interactions provide a molecular mechanism for coupling condensate stability to spatial organization and internal dynamics, enabling sequence heterogeneity and composition to be translated into distinct condensate states.
relevance_reason: Coarse-grained MD simulations of peptide condensates satisfy (a) explicit CG beads, (b) MD methodology, and (c) application to condensate structure and dynamics.

title: Electronic structure and optical properties of antiferromagnetic $3d$-oxides from a Wannier-localized optimally tuned screened range-separated hybrid functional
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander B. Shick, Guy Ohad, Jeffrey B. Neaton, and Leeor Kronik
The authors assess the performance of the recently developed non-empirical Wannier-localized, optimally tuned, screened range-separated hybrid (WOT-SRSH) functional for prototypical antiferromagnetic insulators: MnO, NiO, hematite, and chromia. By comparing WOT-SRSH with established hybrid functionals, self-consistent quasiparticle GW, dynamical mean-field theory, and available experimental data, they demonstrate its ability to offer quantitative improvement in the description of fundamental band gaps, spin magnetic moments, photoemission, and optical spectra. These results establish WOT-SRSH as a promising framework for predictive studies of the electronic, magnetic, and optical properties of magnetic insulators.
[Phys. Rev. Materials 10, 103804] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026
relevance_reason: Benchmarks and applies a Wannier-localized optimally tuned screened range-separated hybrid DFT functional to explicit antiferromagnetic oxides, satisfying (a)-(c) as DFT method development/application.
